_comment: Question bank for bulk AI-answer testing (test_ai_on_bank.py).
Covers Section 11: Trading Platforms + MT5 Mobile Supplement.
20 hard/ambiguous questions targeting confusable wording in the note.

questions.text: The note says MT4 'doesn't support' Stop-Limit orders and separately says MT4 has 'only Limit and Stop' order types. Taken together, how many distinct order types does MT4 have per the note?
options: One combined type called Stop-Limit
Two: Limit and Stop
Three: Limit, Stop, and Stop-Limit
The note doesn't actually specify a number

questions.text: A trader wants to place trades directly from a chart showing a Gold price feed sourced from CME futures data. Which platform's own charting is described as being used for this kind of analysis by most traders?
options: MetaTrader, since it displays charts natively
TradingView, even though execution there depends on broker support
cTrader, since it has a strong server
The Exness Terminal, since it copied TradingView's features

questions.text: Per the note, Expert Advisors are available 'on the desktop version (not on mobile) only.' This restriction is stated for which platform(s)?
options: MetaTrader only
cTrader only
Both MetaTrader and cTrader
All three platforms (MetaTrader, TradingView, cTrader)

questions.text: Which platform does the note explicitly credit with supporting 'custom indicators' in addition to EA-style automation?
options: MetaTrader
TradingView
cTrader
The Exness Terminal

questions.text: The note lists IC Markets both as a TradingView data vendor example and as a broker offering cTrader. Based strictly on the note, which statement is correct?
options: IC Markets is the only broker mentioned that supports both TradingView execution and cTrader
The note never says IC Markets supports TradingView execution, only that its data can be viewed on TradingView charts
IC Markets only supports cTrader, not TradingView in any form
The note states IC Markets exclusively uses the Exness Terminal

questions.text: According to the note, what determines whether a graphical order dragged onto the MT5 chart becomes a Stop or a Limit order?
options: Whether the trader selects Buy or Sell first
The lot size chosen before dragging
Where the line is dropped relative to the current price
Whether it's placed from the Chart tab or the Trade tab

questions.text: The supplement says dragging a line 'above current price sets a Buy Stop.' Based on the note's stated logic (not outside knowledge), what would dragging a line below current price set, if the trader intends to sell?
options: Sell Limit
Sell Stop
The note doesn't cover this case
Buy Limit

questions.text: A position of 0.1 lots is partially closed at 0.05 lots. Per the note, how is this reflected across History views?
options: It appears as a partial in Deals only, never in Orders
It appears as a partial in the History record generally, per the Partial close description
It is merged with the remaining 0.05 in the Positions view but shown separately in the Orders view
Both B and C reflect what the note actually distinguishes

questions.text: Which History view, per the note, would show a single trade's entry and exit combined into one row rather than as separate records?
options: Orders
Deals
Positions
Both Orders and Deals combine them identically

questions.text: The note says MT4 is 'more focused specifically on Forex/currency trading' and 'slowly integrating non-forex instruments,' while MT5 'supports currencies, stock, indices, crypto, metals, basically every instrument.' Does the note state that MT4 cannot trade any non-forex instruments at all?
options: Yes, MT4 is described as forex-only with zero exceptions
No — the note says MT4 is integrating non-forex instruments, just remains forex-focused
The note is silent on whether MT4 supports any non-forex instruments
Yes, only MT5 was ever given non-forex instruments per the note

questions.text: Per the note, connecting a broker in the MT5 app requires navigating through which sequence?
options: Trade tab → Settings → Add Account
Settings → Trade Accounts → "+"
Quotes tab → Edit → "+"
Chart tab → Instrument → Search Broker

questions.text: For an Exness connection in Ethiopia, the note says the trader must select a specific server group name. Which of these matches what the note states, exactly?
options: Exness Ethiopia Ltd
Exness Technologies Ltd
Exness Trade Technologies
Exness Global Ltd

questions.text: Does the note say a trader's demo account password and their real (live) account password are the same, if both are held under one Exness login?
options: Yes, one password covers all sub-accounts
No — each account (demo or real) has its own separate password
The note doesn't mention demo account passwords at all
Only real accounts get separate passwords; demo shares the main login

questions.text: The note distinguishes the Quotes tab's ask/bid display. Per the note, which is shown larger and in which position?
options: Bid, top-right
Ask, top-right
Ask, bottom-left
Both are shown the same size, just in different corners

questions.text: cTrader is described as being 'recommended particularly for people using ECN accounts and scalpers.' Does the note claim cTrader is required for ECN accounts, or only broker-dependent?
options: Required — ECN accounts cannot function without cTrader
Broker-dependent — the note says 'if your broker allows it'
The note doesn't connect cTrader to broker availability at all
cTrader is described as mandatory only for scalpers, optional for ECN

questions.text: Which of these does the note NOT list as something you can do via the Exness Terminal or Exness App, according to Section 3?
options: View Exness-branded charting that copied TradingView's features
Execute orders directly
Code Expert Advisors using Exness's own scripting language
Trade without using MetaTrader, cTrader, or TradingView at all

questions.text: The note claims MT5 was launched 'around 2010' and MT4 'around 2005.' If a broker in 2007 only offered one MetaTrader platform, which one would it most plausibly have been, based purely on the note's stated timeline?
options: MT5, since it's the more advanced one
MT4, since MT5 wouldn't have existed yet per the stated dates
Either — the note says they launched simultaneously
Neither — the note states brokers only adopted MetaTrader after 2010

questions.text: The note states MetaTrader platforms are used 'only for execution purposes' and 'not typically used for chart analysis, even though they have charts.' What does this imply about MetaTrader's charting capability itself?
options: MetaTrader has no charting feature at all
MetaTrader does have charts, but they aren't the tool most traders rely on for analysis
MetaTrader's charts are only visible on desktop, not mobile
MetaTrader removed charting starting with MT5

questions.text: In the Trade tab, batch controls exist to close positions in bulk. Per the note, what are the two batch options available?
options: Close all pending orders / close all market orders
Close all losing positions / close all profitable positions
Close all Buy positions / close all Sell positions
Close all Orders view entries / close all Deals view entries

questions.text: Considering both the main note and the supplement together, which statement best reflects what the note says about where Expert Advisors can be built or used in MT5?
options: Only within the mobile app's Chart tab, using the drawing tool
On the desktop version only, using MetaTrader's own coding language — not described as available in the mobile walkthrough
Anywhere the app is installed, since EAs sync across devices
Only through the Settings tab where accounts are added
